game_title: Go Teacher v5 · synthetic interface test
overall_feedback: This page uses deterministic test-engine data to check the lesson interface. The numbers are synthetic, not a review of a real game.

game_arc.intro: A test fixture for the complete report-to-lesson path.

phases.narrative: The record exercises board setup, engine evidence and two human perspectives.

lessons.title: Read the next reply
lessons.story: This example checks that the board follows the game record and starts each variation from the right position.
lessons.principle: Before choosing your move, consider the opponent’s reply.

panels.position: First inspect the position, then choose a panel.
panels.played: Follow the consequence of the played move. Change perspective to see a sampled human continuation.
panels.best: Compare the engine’s preferred plan with the played move.
panels.local: A local search is limited evidence; it does not prove that a group is alive or dead.
panels.what_if: These are separate sampled futures. Later decisions also contribute to the final score difference.

puzzles.title: Count before you play elsewhere
puzzles.hint: Which liberty belongs to both black stones?
puzzles.explanation: D2 connects to both stones and gives the chain more liberties. This prevents the immediate capture.

wrong_moves.explanation: White fills the chain’s last liberty at D2 and captures B2 and C2.

puzzles.generic_wrong_explanation: Check the shared liberty before playing elsewhere.

source.title: British Go Association — capturing and liberties

puzzles.transformation: Synthetic regression example of the tutorial’s atari motif: use a two-stone chain with a shared escape point. This fixture tests playback, not puzzle difficulty.
puzzles.verification: Replayed captures and counted the chain’s liberties before and after D2; the goal is to avoid immediate capture, not prove unconditional life.
puzzles.transfer_explanation: Read the opponent’s immediate capture before choosing a move elsewhere.
